title: Resume Maker Latex
shortDescription: Production-grade Web App software engineering system implemented in TypeScript, JavaScript. Features a decoupled multi-tier architecture with validated API endpoints and resilient state processing.
description: **Resume Maker LaTeX** is a full‑stack **MERN‑style** application that lets authenticated users create, edit, and download professional resumes. The backend, built with `Express` and `TypeScript`, secures all routes with JWT authentication and stores rich resume data in **MongoDB** via **Mongoose** models. The frontend, powered by **React 18**, **Vite**, **TailwindCSS**, and **Shadcn UI**, offers a dark‑mode, desktop‑first experience (packaged with **Electron**) with real‑time preview, drag‑and‑drop ordering (`dnd-kit`), and rich‑text editing (`Tiptap`). PDF generation is handled both by **PDFKit** and a LaTeX pipeline (`node‑latex`), exposing dedicated download endpoints.
longDescription:
The system follows a **layered architecture**: the presentation layer (React SPA) communicates with a RESTful API layer (`/api/auth/*` and `/api/resumes/*`) over HTTPS. Each request passes through an `isAuthenticated` middleware that validates JWT tokens, applies **Helmet** security headers, and enforces rate‑limiting to mitigate brute‑force attacks. *Data ingestion* begins at the controller level where incoming payloads are validated against **Joi** schemas before being persisted to MongoDB. Resume documents contain sanitized HTML generated by **Tiptap**, ensuring XSS safety via server‑side sanitization.

When a user triggers a download, the controller delegates to a service that either streams a **PDFKit** document or invokes the **LaTeX** compiler (`node‑latex`). The compiled PDF or `.tex` source is streamed back to the client, allowing instant preview or offline editing. The frontend leverages **React Query** for caching and optimistic UI updates, while the drag‑and‑drop UI (`dnd-kit`) synchronously updates the resume's section order in the database, handling rapid re‑ordering edge cases.

**Security guardrails** include JWT token rotation, HTTP‑only cookies, and strict CORS policies. All routes are protected by the `isAuthenticated` middleware, and sensitive operations (e.g., resume deletion) are logged for audit. The build topology uses **Vite** for fast HMR in development and produces a production bundle that is bundled into an Electron executable, delivering native‑like performance while retaining web flexibility.

The deployment pipeline (not fully detailed in the code) is designed for **continuous integration** with automated linting, TypeScript compilation, and unit tests (future work). The repository also contains scripts for **MongoDB Atlas** connection pooling and graceful shutdown handling, ensuring resilience in production environments.
myContributions: Implemented JWT‑based authentication with refresh token flow and integrated it across all protected routes
Created Express routers and controllers for full CRUD lifecycle of resumes, including secure download endpoints
Integrated `node‑latex` for on‑the‑fly LaTeX compilation and PDF streaming
Designed and wired a drag‑and‑drop UI using `dnd-kit` that synchronizes order indices with MongoDB
Sanitized and persisted rich‑text HTML from `Tiptap` to prevent XSS attacks
Configured Helmet, CORS, and rate‑limiting middleware to harden API surface
Set up Mongoose models and Joi validation schemas for strict data contracts
Packaged the React frontend into an Electron desktop application for native‑like performance
Implemented React Query caching and optimistic updates for a snappy user experience
Added comprehensive error handling and graceful shutdown logic for MongoDB connections

features: User registration, login, and JWT‑protected session management
CRUD operations for resumes (create, read, update, delete)
Real‑time preview of resume content with rich‑text editing
Drag‑and‑drop reordering of resume sections with immediate persistence
LaTeX PDF generation and source `.tex` download
Dark‑mode UI built with TailwindCSS and Shadcn UI components
Rate limiting and security headers via Helmet
challenges: Balancing real‑time drag‑and‑drop UI responsiveness with database write consistency, especially under rapid user actions
Ensuring XSS‑free storage of HTML generated by Tiptap while preserving formatting
Managing two separate PDF generation pipelines (PDFKit vs LaTeX) without code duplication
Handling LaTeX compilation errors gracefully and providing useful feedback to the user
Coordinating JWT token refresh flow across Electron’s main and renderer processes
learnings: Deepened expertise in Electron IPC patterns for secure communication between main and renderer processes
Mastered integration of headless UI primitives (Shadcn/Radix) for fully customizable components
Refined backend validation using Joi before persisting to Mongoose, reducing runtime errors
Learned to orchestrate LaTeX compilation in a Node environment using `node‑latex`
Improved strategies for optimistic UI updates and conflict resolution in drag‑and‑drop scenarios
